summary: K. Kanapathypillai (1902–1968) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Hartley College and the University of London (circa 1936–1940) and later taught Alvappillai Veluppillai.

K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned PhDs from the University of Madras and University of London (under John Brough), and held posts at Madras, the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist. She earned her PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under Madhukar Anant Mehendale, and held an attested post at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 1983.

K. N. Jayatilleke (1920–1970) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at the University of Cambridge, and served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon.

K. R. Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who earned his M.A. at Downing College, Cambridge. He taught at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and served as President of the Pali Text Society (1981–1994).

K. S. Balasubramanian is an Indologist and philosopher. He has held posts at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, serving as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Director (attested 2026).

id: P:K. S. J. M. de Vreese
summary: K. S. J. M. de Vreese (born 1906) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as a privaat-docent at Leiden University from 1948 and became an extraordinary professor at the University of Amsterdam in 1960.

K. Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

K. V. Puttappa (1904–1994) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore. He later taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

K. V. Raman (1934–2024) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College, the University of Madras, and the Institute of Archaeology. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India and was Professor and Head at the University of Madras.

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1981–1987) and as Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Yongtong Tang, Sentian Wang, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, earned a Doctor of Letters from Visva-Bharati University, and held a teaching post there.

Kaie Mochizuki (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has held academic posts at Minobusan University, serving as professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and university president (attested 2026).
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyo Mitomo. He served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaigyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg and served as principal of Shiba Junior & Senior High School and professor at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho universities.

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Komazawa and Keio universities. He lectured at Harvard University (circa 1913–1915) and served as the first president of Komazawa University (1925–1934).
Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Otani University, where he served as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002).

Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Sogen Omori, later holding a post at Sophia University from circa 1966 to 1996.

Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, where he later taught from circa 1923 to 1955 after an earlier post at Scottish Church College.

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied at Palpung Monastery under Drupon Norbu Dondrup, served there as Vajra Master (circa 1943–1955), became abbot of Jangchub Choeling Monastery in 1957, and founded Samdrup Thargye Ling.
